risk_if_not_implemented: Without Dual Authorization for Sensitive / Regulated Data Destruction, users, services and processes may obtain or retain access beyond authorized need, enabling misuse or escalation. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss, Theft or Damage of Assets (R-AM-1), Data Loss / Integrity Compromise (R-BC-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct (MT-14), Conflict of Interest (COI) / Undue Influence / Insider Misconduct (MT-15).

compensating_control_1.name: Digital & Non-Digital Media Disposal
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to securely dispose of, destroy and/or erase digital and non-digital media when it is no longer required, using organization-defined procedures.
compensating_control_1.justification: Digital & Non-Digital Media Disposal (DCH-17) provides physical access control that compensates for the absence of Dual Authorization for Sensitive Data Destruction (DCH-17.1) by preventing unauthorized physical interaction with systems and infrastructure. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Secure Disposal, Destruction or Re-Use of Equipment
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to securely dispose of, destroy or repurpose technology assets using organization-defined techniques and methods to prevent:
(1) Data recovery; and
(2) Components from being resold, redistributed and/or reused through unauthorized channels.
compensating_control_2.justification: Secure Disposal, Destruction or Re-Use of Equipment (AST-22) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Dual Authorization for Sensitive Data Destruction (DCH-17.1) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
